teams.heading: Danford says Fiji deaf rugby sevens teams still need up to $70,000
teams.body: Earlier this month, team manager Lionel Danford told the Fiji Sun that Fiji's men's and women's deaf rugby sevens teams still need between $50,000 and $70,000 for the World Deaf Rugby Sevens Championship in Tokyo. Kit has been funded, but daily expenses and camp preparation still need money. "We are still looking for funds," Danford said. Consistent player numbers, particularly in the women's squad, are another problem, with many players unemployed and paying their own transport to training.

lead.why: The only fresh Fiji item in the pack that is not the Byrne exit or the Coca-Cola cans, and it has a named source and a concrete funding figure.

teams.heading: Ollie Sleightholme hat-trick boosts England November Test case in Premiership
teams.body: In Premiership club action, Ollie Sleightholme's hat-trick helped Northampton beat Bath 71-48 at Franklin's Gardens, and it may be enough to push his case for the November Tests. He managed 151 metres from 10 carries, beat 11 defenders and made four linebreaks, a throwback to the form that carried him into the Test picture in 2024. Alex Coles also scored for the Saints, and the England lock's display will leave Steve Borthwick beaming.

lead.why: A club-form story with a direct England selection angle ahead of the November Tests, not already covered in the edition series.

teams.heading: France 'ready to join' Springboks and All Blacks as third superpower
teams.body: A piece on MSN argues France are ready to join the Springboks and All Blacks as rugby's third superpower. The record gives that claim some support: France have won two and lost one of three Nations Championship games, most recently beating Japan 42-15 in Round 3, and sit third of 12 on the log. Fiji come next in Round 4, the first real test of whether the argument holds.

lead.why: It is the only shortlisted item not already reported, and it is a live argument about France's standing in the game.

teams.heading: Ireland women's Aoife Wafer ruled out of South Africa WXV trip
teams.body: Ireland women's Aoife Wafer has been ruled out of the WXV Global Series trip to South Africa, after the 23-year-old Harlequins player sustained what the Irish Rugby Football Union called a "minor injury in training". Wafer missed the wins over Japan in Galway and Cork and will not travel with head coach Scott Bemand's 30-player squad for the Tests against the Springbok Women in Cape Town. Ruth Campbell returns from an ankle injury to make the squad, while Sam Monaghan remains out with an Achilles problem.

lead.why: A fresh injury blow to a named player, not yet covered in the tab's editions, and the strongest genuinely new item in the pack.

teams.heading: Italy's highest world ranking is No. 8, reached in 2007 and 2024
teams.body: Italy's best world ranking is No. 8, reached in 2007 and again in 2024. In the Nations Championship so far, the Azzurri have won none of three matches, losing all three, with 37 points scored and 131 conceded for a difference of -94. Their most recent outing was a 10-57 defeat by Australia in Round 3, and the next match is against South Africa in Round 4.

teams.heading: Scotland risk losing Hector Patterson as Bath track England-eligible Edinburgh scrum-half
teams.body: This club transfer story, first reported on 3 October, has Bath understood to be monitoring Edinburgh scrum-half Hector Patterson, whose contract runs only to the end of the season. The 21-year-old, son of former Scotland scrum-half Derrick Patterson, is also eligible for England through a grandparent, and The Times reported leading English and French clubs are interested. No deal has been agreed and Patterson remains an Edinburgh player. With the 2027 World Cup a year away, his next move matters for Scotland.

lead.why: It is the only item in the pack with a named Scotland-relevant player and a live allegiance question, though it is a week old and club-level.

teams.heading: Premiership: Tommy Reffell presses Wales case in Leicester's 38-31 win over Gloucester
teams.body: In Friday's Premiership match, Leicester came from 14 points down to beat Gloucester 38-31 at Welford Road, with Tommy Reffell a constant nuisance at the breakdown. Planet Rugby reckons the flanker pressed his case for a Wales starting jersey ahead of next month's Nations Championship block, and his try-saving tackle on Will Joseph in the 65th minute was vital. Aaron Wainwright, also a Wales international, scored his first try for the club.

lead.why: A new Premiership story with a Wales angle on Reffell's push for a starting jersey, not a repeat of the three editions already run.

teams.heading: Shaun Edwards starts Pumas duties late, after Red Roses WXV commitments
teams.body: Shaun Edwards will not start work with Argentina until the end of October, as he remains a consultant to the Red Roses until the WXV Global Series ends on October 30. He then joins Felipe Contepomi's staff for the November Nations Championship matches against Ireland, Italy and France, on a contract that runs to the end of the 2027 World Cup. BBC Sport reports the appointment ends speculation of a role under Steve Borthwick at England, and he left France earlier this year.

lead.why: It is the only shortlist item marked NEW, and it adds timing detail (the Red Roses consultancy and the start date) that the earlier editions did not carry.

teams.heading: Len Ikitau ruled out of Bledisloe rematch; Toole, Pritchard called up
teams.body: Len Ikitau's concussion has ruled him out of Saturday's second Bledisloe Cup Test in Sydney, leaving the Wallabies searching for a centres partner for Isaac Henry. Ikitau left the field in the first half at Eden Park after a head knock, failed his HIA and will serve the mandatory stand-down period. Jordan Petaia (ankle) is also out. Brumbies duo Corey Toole and Kadin Pritchard have joined the squad, and Pritchard, who started 12 games at outside centre for the Brumbies this year, could make his Wallabies debut.

lead.why: A new injury and squad change for the Sydney rematch, not previously reported, with Ikitau's concussion ruling a material development.

teams.heading: Japan women's Sakura XV lose again to Ireland, leave Europe winless
teams.body: Japan's women's Sakura XV lost 19-43 to Ireland in Cork, their second defeat to the same side in a week, and finish the European leg winless in four straight matches. Japan had the early territory and Sakurako Korai's rolling-maul try put them ahead, but Ireland's scrum pressure and kicking game, led by Dannah O'Brien, gave the Sakura problems, and Ireland scored three tries to lead 22-7. The Sakura return home to face Wales twice in the WXV Global Series.

lead.why: The Sakura XV's second straight loss to Ireland is a fresh women's story that hasn't run in this edition series, and today's shortlist has no fresher men's item.

teams.heading: Leroy Carter in doubt for Sydney after injury in Eden Park rout
teams.body: Saturday's first Bledisloe Cup Test at Eden Park added to Dave Rennie's injury list. Winger Leroy Carter was hurt as he scored in the 50-19 win and is now in doubt for next Saturday's second Test at Accor Stadium in Sydney. Scott Barrett failed a head injury assessment on his return, and Anton Segner left with a head wound after a collision with a team-mate. The coverage has no update on any of the three, which leaves Sydney's selection picture unclear.

lead.why: The match review carries the sharpest new development: three injuries from Saturday's win, which the Bledisloe coverage has not yet been followed by any update on.

teams.heading: Springboks keep No. 1 as All Blacks trim gap to 1.28 points
teams.body: South Africa remain top of the World Rugby rankings on 93.09, but New Zealand's 50-19 thrashing of Australia at Eden Park has closed the gap to just over a point. The All Blacks rose from 91.15 to 91.81, and a margin that stood at almost four points has narrowed significantly. Planet Rugby judges the Boks face the tougher November road, with trips to Ireland and France in the Nations Championship, so the No. 1 spot will be tested before the year is out.

lead.why: It is a fresh competitive-status story that matters to South Africa's stake at No. 1, and it is not the Bulls v Lions match already covered today.
